ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 15 V DC unregulated power supply; the positive terminal of the power supply is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to a Zener diode reference node labeled Vz = 3 V, and this node is connected to the + input terminal of the operational amplifier. On the right side are the pass transistor and the regulated output terminal; the output terminal is connected back to the - input terminal of the operational amplifier through a feedback voltage-divider network, in which the upper-arm resistor is 40 kΩ, the lower-arm resistor is 20 kΩ, and the lower end of the 20 kΩ is grounded. Reasoning: Under negative-feedback voltage regulation operation, the ideal op amp makes the voltage at the - input terminal equal to the voltage at the + input terminal, that is, the voltage at the midpoint of the feedback divider is 3 V. The voltage-divider relationship is 3 = Vout × 20/(40 + 20). Therefore Vout = 3 × 60/20 = 9 V.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that the op-amp's + input is held at the 3 V Zener reference. Then identify the feedback divider from the regulated output: 40 kΩ on top and 20 kΩ to ground, with the divider midpoint feeding the op-amp's - input. Apply negative feedback, so the divider midpoint must also be 3 V. Set 3 = Vout * 20/(40+20), giving Vout = 3 * 60/20 = 9 V.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct closed-loop feedback analysis using the visible Zener reference and the feedback divider; this is the natural single solution route for this circuit.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit diagram: a 15 V DC unregulated source feeds a regulator; the non-inverting op-amp input is tied to a Zener reference labeled Vz = 3 V; the inverting input is connected to the midpoint of a divider with 40 kΩ from the regulated output to the midpoint and 20 kΩ from the midpoint to the negative/ground rail; the op-amp drives a pass transistor whose output node is the regulated DC output.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know that the required quantity is the regulated power supply output voltage in volts.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use ideal op-amp negative feedback: in regulation, V- equals V+; the feedback midpoint voltage is the divider fraction Vout * 20 kΩ/(40 kΩ + 20 kΩ). The pass transistor voltage drop is inside the feedback loop, so it does not change the setpoint calculation.
